subtype: Approach: bringing in a trusted mentor as mediator [Action]
passage:
Hansa: Just left Rao uncle's office. That exercise was so odd 😅
Abhinav: Saying your side out loud was the weird part. I said you want the larger share because you built the first version.
Hansa: And I had to say you want it split evenly because you quit your job first and took the bigger risk.
Abhinav: You got it right. Weirdly, that helped.
Hansa: He looked at both of us and said he'd bring options only after that.
Abhinav: Rao uncle ran his own company for years. I trust him to be fair.
Hansa: Same. He'll send three options tomorrow.
Abhinav: I'll read them properly this time, not just hunt for what's wrong.
Hansa: Deal. Tea tomorrow to go through them? 🙂

qa.q: What did Rao uncle ask each founder to do before offering options?
qa.a: Rao uncle asked each founder to say the other's side out loud.

qa.q: Why did Abhinav say "Weirdly, that helped"?
qa.a: Abhinav felt heard and a little relieved, because Hansa described the quitting-a-job risk correctly.

qa.q: What could the founders do if none of Rao uncle's three options felt fair?
qa.a: They could ask Rao uncle to explain the thinking behind each option, then say back what they would change and why.

qa.q: How might Hansa have felt about having to restate Abhinav's view?
qa.a: Hansa felt awkward at first, shown by the 😅, but came out calmer and ready for tea, which suggests the exercise softened things.

grounding: The chat shows co-founders bringing in a senior friend who asks each to restate the other's view before proposing options on equity.
